chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When a man says to his wife, 'I did not find you a virgin,' and he has no proof, he is flogged with the ta'zir punishment, and he is kept apart from her; this does not contradict the earlier reports, because the meaning of his statement 'he is flogged with the punishment' refers to the discretionary punishment (ta'zir), and he did not mean a complete (fixed) punishment, as indicated by the preceding reports.

key_terms.يُجْلَدُ الْحَدَّ: he is flogged with the punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a husband who accuses his wife of not being a virgin without proof?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal distinction between *hadd* (fixed punishment) and *ta'zir* (discretionary punishment) in the context of a husband accusing his wife of non-virginity (*laman*) without proof. The Imam emphasizes that the phrase 'flogged with the penalty' refers specifically to *ta'zir*, thereby maintaining the marital bond and aligning with earlier established narrations. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach of interpreting linguistic cues in light of comprehensive hadith evidence to determine the precise nature of the punishment.
